Verified 6 evidence-backed findings across all specialist agents.

threats.title: Authentication Token Forgery & Identity Spoofing
threats.description: Adversaries may forge or tamper with authentication bearer tokens or session cookies to impersonate legitimate users.
threats.potential_impact: Full account takeover and unauthorized transactional capability.
threats.mitigation_strategy: Enforce cryptographically strong asymmetric signatures (RS256/Ed25519) on all JWTs, strictly forbid 'none' algorithm, and rotate signing keys periodically.

threats.title: Input Parameter Manipulation & Query Tampering
threats.description: Unsanitized query parameters or request bodies could allow adversaries to tamper with database queries or application state.
threats.potential_impact: Unauthorized data modification, unauthorized balance alteration, or state corruption.
threats.mitigation_strategy: Enforce strict Pydantic/JSON schema validation on all inputs; utilize parameterized ORM queries; apply cryptographic HMACs for stateful parameters.

threats.title: Insufficient Transaction Audit Logging & Non-Repudiation Deficit
threats.description: State-altering API calls may lack tamper-evident forensic logging, allowing malicious actors to deny performing actions.
threats.potential_impact: Inability to trace forensic origin of data manipulation, failed compliance audits, disputed chargebacks.
threats.mitigation_strategy: Implement append-only, cryptographically hashed audit trails for sensitive operations capturing timestamp, user ID, client IP, and request digest.

threats.title: Technology Stack Fingerprinting & Verbose Error Leakage
threats.description: Server response headers, stack traces, and unauthenticated metadata endpoints disclose underlying framework and runtime versions.
threats.potential_impact: Assists attackers in tailoring zero-day exploits targeting exact component versions.
threats.mitigation_strategy: Strip 'Server' and 'X-Powered-By' headers in reverse proxy configs; disable detailed exception stack dumps in production environments.

threats.title: Unthrottled API Resource Exhaustion & Heavy Query DoS
threats.description: Lack of explicit rate-limiting tokens allows concurrent high-frequency queries to exhaust backend threads and database connection pools.
threats.potential_impact: Application downtime, degraded SLA, resource starvation for legitimate users.
threats.mitigation_strategy: Deploy leaky-bucket or token-bucket rate limiting (e.g. Redis sliding window) at the API gateway layer.

threats.title: Horizontal & Vertical Role Authorization Bypass
threats.description: Administrative endpoints or object identifiers may not consistently enforce server-side Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
threats.potential_impact: Unprivileged actors executing administrative actions, data wiping, and system reconfiguration.
threats.mitigation_strategy: Adopt centralized authorization policy middleware; enforce Principle of Least Privilege across all route handlers.

threat_model.architectural_summary: STRIDE Threat Analysis for dld.srmist.edu.in identified 6 structural threat vectors across 25 mapped attack surfaces. Priority attention is required for 7 high-risk data and administrative endpoints.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) to Cloud Metadata
findings.description: The server accepts arbitrary external URLs and queries them from within the trusted backend network boundary.
findings.plain_english_summary: The web server acts as an obedient proxy for the attacker. If the attacker tells it to fetch an address, it will fetch it—even if that address is a secret internal cloud management server that normal internet users can't reach.
findings.where_is_the_flaw: Endpoint 'GET https://dld.srmist.edu.in/api/fetch' at parameter 'url'. The server makes HTTP requests to user-supplied web addresses without restricting internal private IP spaces.
findings.how_attacker_exploits:
1. Attacker sets the 'url' parameter to 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/'.
2. The server queries the internal AWS/GCP instance metadata endpoint on behalf of the attacker.
3. The response contains temporary IAM admin credentials, secret keys, and internal network IP lists.
findings.real_world_impact: Cloud Infrastructure Takeover: Exposure of cloud IAM keys, unauthorized access to private databases, and lateral movement across the entire virtual network.
reproduction_steps: Request endpoint specifying cloud metadata destination
Inspect response containing cloud IAM or instance credentials
findings.remediation_advice: Implement strict URL allowlisting, block private IP address spaces, and enforce IMDSv2 token authentication.
findings.remediation_code_sample:
# Secure Implementation (IP Range Validation):
import ipaddress
ip = ipaddress.ip_address(resolved_ip)
if ip.is_private or ip.is_loopback:
    raise SecurityException("Internal IP access denied")

findings.title: Unauthenticated Access to Administrative Endpoint: https://dld.srmist.edu.in/admin
findings.description: Privileged administrative endpoint is accessible anonymously without authentication or RBAC validation.
findings.plain_english_summary: The admin control panel has no lock on the front door. Anyone who knows or guesses the URL can enter and use management functions without entering any password or logging in.
findings.where_is_the_flaw: Endpoint 'GET https://dld.srmist.edu.in/admin'. The route handler lacks authentication and role-based access control (RBAC) middleware, allowing open anonymous internet traffic to reach management functions.
findings.how_attacker_exploits:
1. Attacker discovers the admin endpoint via directory brute-forcing or automated scanning.
2. Attacker sends a direct request without any authorization headers.
3. The application grants unrestricted access to privileged operations, user lists, and internal system configs.
findings.real_world_impact: Full Administrative Compromise: Unauthorized management of users, backend configurations, system status, and internal operational data.
reproduction_steps: Send GET request directly to https://dld.srmist.edu.in/admin with zero credentials
Verify administrative operations or internal configurations are exposed
findings.remediation_advice: Enforce role-based access control (RBAC) middleware on all administrative route groups.

findings.title: Missing Critical Security Hardening Headers: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Content-Type-Options
findings.description: The application responds without critical security defenses (Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Content-Type-Options), increasing susceptibility to clickjacking and MIME-type sniffing.
findings.plain_english_summary: The server is missing browser security shield instructions. These headers tell browsers not to allow other websites to frame your site inside an invisible window (clickjacking) or guess file types dangerously.
findings.where_is_the_flaw: HTTP response headers on base URL 'https://dld.srmist.edu.in'. The web server configuration is missing defensive HTTP headers: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.how_attacker_exploits:
1. Attacker embeds your website in an invisible iframe on a malicious webpage (Clickjacking).
2. The attacker tricks a logged-in user into clicking buttons on the overlay, unknowingly performing transactions or altering account settings.
findings.real_world_impact: Clickjacking & MIME Spoofing: Users can be tricked into performing unintended state changes, or browsers can be tricked into executing malicious scripts via MIME confusion.
reproduction_steps: Inspect response headers to verify absence of CSP, X-Frame-Options, or X-Content-Type-Options
